title: The four categories this archive is sorted into
purpose: Every countable item in this archive belongs to exactly one of four categories. The category says who made the thing, not what shape the thing is.
approved_by: the four section names are the plan's: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-full-recovery-v6.md Task 8a ('A Works by Asadullah Ali / B Contributions & Collaborations / C Interviews, Reception & Mentions About Him / D Other Materials'). The plan was approved via grilling rounds 1-3 on 2026-09-27. The PAGE RENDERINGS of this taxonomy have NOT yet been put to the site owner: that is the Task 9 gate, and the published counts are still the pre-recount ones.
built_by: scripts/apply_taxonomy.py stamps `category` and `counted` on every row of the data files named in `data_files`; run it with --check to verify the assignment without writing. The rule each file is held to is recorded in that script and in the per-file `note` below, so the assignment is reproducible from the repository instead of resting on one ad-hoc run.
ordering_rule: Categorise by AUTHORSHIP, not by format. A video he produced is A even if it is a debate, a lecture, or a call-in show. A show he was a guest on is C even though it carries his voice, his name in the title, and his argument.

categories.label: Works by Asadullah Ali
includes: Every row of canonical_works.json: the works he wrote for his own sites (72 rows).
The video productions he made himself: the numbered episodes of The Andalusian Project series, archived on archive.org, plus any third-party mirror of a recording he produced.
Papers he authored alone: every papers.json row whose co_authors list is empty.
MDI rows carrying counted_as_work: true, i.e. a distinct item of content published once (4 of the 17 rows).
excludes: A second publication of a work already counted (13 MDI rows): catalogued, uncounted, and pointed at the counted work by duplicate_of.
A recording produced by someone else in which he appears (category C).
A paper he wrote with someone else (category B).

categories.label: Contributions & Collaborations
includes: Papers carrying a non-empty co_authors field: written with one or more named co-authors.
Works whose provenance records joint production rather than sole authorship.
excludes: A record he only appeared in, however central he was to it: a debate he spoke in is C unless he produced it, and a co-written paper is B.
Items that are catalogued but never counted (notices, link-outs, the derived secondary_sources).

categories.label: Interviews, Reception & Mentions About Him
categories.short: He is the guest or the subject
includes: His appearances in other people's shows: debate recordings uploaded by the Muslim Debate Initiative, MSA Ohio State, and other channels, plus translated and clipped excerpts of those appearances.
Reprints, critiques, biographies and passing mentions written by others about him.
The 70 rows of secondary_sources.json, which are DERIVED from the archive's own data and therefore never counted as content.
excludes: A recording he made himself, even one that answers or criticises another person's claim: that is A.
The link-out rows (category D), which record a link rather than an appearance.

categories.label: Other Materials
includes: Notices: announcements rather than works (3 rows).
Link-outs: the conversion-story reprint, held as metadata only, and 9 Yaqeen pages whose text is never downloaded by this project (10 rows).
Site and channel history material: what the site and channel were, when they went offline, and which figures about them are refused.
excludes: Anything with recovered text that is counted: the archive never files real content in D to keep it out of a total.

rules.one_category_per_item: A thing counted in two buckets is a bug. Every countable item carries exactly one category letter and counted: true, and every uncounted row carries counted: false.
rules.never_counted: Every row of secondary_sources.json, of notices.json and of linkouts.json is catalogued but NEVER counted. They are listed so a reader can see they exist; they add nothing to any total. The row counts those files carry are stated in `data_files` below, and scripts/apply_taxonomy.py --check fails if any of them drifts from the data.
rules.format_is_not_authorship: A debate he produced is A. A show he was a guest on is C. An interview he conducted is A because he made the recording. A paper he co-wrote is B. Never decide a category by the word 'interview', 'dialogue' or 'debate' in a title.
rules.guest_vs_producer: The test is who made the recording, read off the entry's own evidence (its archive_url host, its uploader named in source, its title, its note). A YouTube upload on somebody else's channel is their production unless the entry's own evidence says he produced the recording.
rules.duplicates_are_not_a_fifth_place: A second publication of a work already counted (13 MDI rows) keeps its category letter for orientation, but carries counted: false and duplicate_of, so the count still lands in exactly one bucket.
rules.counts_are_computed: No page may type a number. The homepage counts each category by counting rows in the data at build time.
rules.ambiguity: Where the entry's own evidence does not settle authorship, the item is assigned A, a category_basis string records why it was ambiguous, and the entry is listed for the controller in the Task 8a report. Guessing silently is not allowed.

canonical_works.json.note: All 72. No work row records joint production, so none is B. apostasy-beyond-the-rhetoric was first published on islamicdiscourseinitiative.com rather than asadullahali.com but is still his sole byline.

videos.json.category: A or C by the entry's own evidence
videos.json.note: 57 A, 11 C. No entry carries kind: lecture, so the rule fell to the evidence on each entry: archive.org items of his own numbered series are A; a show he was a guest on is C.

papers.json.category: A if co_authors is empty, B otherwise
papers.json.note: 17 A, 3 B. The type field is a format label (Talk, Interview, Conference Paper) and never decides the category.

mdi_articles.json.counted: counted_as_work: true on 4 rows, false on 13
mdi_articles.json.note: All 17 carry category A because the byline is his; the 13 that republish an already-counted work are counted: false and name the work they duplicate in duplicate_of.

secondary_sources.json.note: Derived from the archive's own catalogue (mention, bio, reprint, critique). count_as_content is already false on every row; counted: false added for the same statement in one field name.

notices.json.note: Announcements, not works. counted_as_work was already false; counted: false added.

linkouts.json.note: 1 conversion-story reprint held as metadata only, 9 Yaqeen pages. No text was downloaded for any of them, so no size is counted.

channel_facts.json.note: Site and channel history material. Owned by another agent; read only, never written here. Rendered on its own page at /channel/.
